Cleary Gottlieb is a pioneer in globalizing the legal profession. We have 14 offices in major financial centers around the world, but we operate as a single, integrated global partnership and not as a U.S. firm with a network of overseas locations. Since 1946 our lawyers and staff have worked across practices, industries, jurisdictions, and continents to provide clients with simple, actionable approaches to their most complex legal and business challenges, whether domestic or international. We support every client relationship with intellectual agility, commercial acumen, and a human touch.
We're an internal team at Cleary Gottlieb building bespoke AI solutions for legal work, drawing on software engineering, data science, and deep domain expertise. We work at the boundary of enterprise-grade software, and we are regularly building services and applications nobody here has built before. That makes for a dynamic learning environment — and one where a junior engineer will gain exposure to real-world AI systems from day one.

Junior engineers are paired with experienced mentors and participate in structured code reviews, pair-programming sessions, and weekly knowledge-sharing stand-ups.

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.
The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Connectivity Software Engineering Intern
Embedded Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Access
Software Engineering Intern - Embedded Systems

Role Summary
At RV Tech, we develop next-gen vehicle features that include remote commands from mobile apps, OTA software updates, real time vehicle telemetry, and fleet management tools. All of which rely on cloud, connectivity, and integration software working together at scale. As a Connected Systems intern, you will work on the backend services, integration layers, or connectivity infrastructure that keep vehicles talking to the cloud reliably. This may involve high throughput data pipelines, distributed cloud services, or the software that validates features work end to end across the vehicle.
Specific Project Areas Vary By Team And May Include
Building and testing backend services that process vehicle telemetry and remote commands at fleet scale
Developing event driven, distributed systems using tools such as Kafka, Kinesis, or Redis
Contributing to cross domain systems integration and validation work, ensuring vehicle features function correctly end to end
Supporting connectivity infrastructure, including the messaging and communication layers linking vehicle, mobile app, and cloud
Working with cloud native infrastructure on AWS (EKS, Lambda, DynamoDB, IoT Core)
Responsibilities
Design, develop, and test software components within an existing distributed or connectivity system
Write clean, maintainable code in Python, Go, C++, or Java depending on the team
Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and debugging sessions with your team
Contribute to test automation and validation for integration or connectivity features
Document your work and present progress to your team throughout the internship
Qualifications
Minimum:
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university
Proficient in at least one of Python, Go, C++, or Java
Preferred
Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship
Exposure to distributed systems, event driven architecture, or cloud platforms, AWS preferred
Familiarity with vehicle communication protocols such as CAN or MQTT, or IoT concepts
Coursework or project experience with backend development, systems integration, or test automation
Total Rewards
We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program.

You will work closely with software engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to improve test coverage, identify risks early, and support the delivery of high-quality software.
Software Development Engineer In Test – Role Overview
As a Software Development Engineer in Test, you will design, develop, and maintain automated test frameworks and test suites across web, API, and service-based applications. You will contribute to the full software development lifecycle, from test planning and risk assessment through to execution, defect analysis, and release validation.
Key Responsibilities
Design, develop, and maintain robust automated test frameworks and test suites using suitable programming languages, tools, and testing patterns.
Create and execute automated and exploratory tests for functional, integration, regression, system, API, 508 and end-to-end testing.
Develop and maintain mobile test automation for native, hybrid, or mobile web applications using tools such as Appium or equivalent technologies.
Work with developers, product managers, and delivery teams to understand requirements, identify acceptance criteria, and define effective test strategies.
Analyse user stories, technical designs, and product risks to identify test scenarios, edge cases, and potential failure modes.
Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines and provide timely, reliable feedback on build and release quality.
Investigate test failures, reproduce defects, perform root cause analysis, and collaborate with engineering teams to drive issues through to resolution.
Maintain clear test documentation, automation standards, defect records, and quality metrics.
Review code and test automation contributions, promoting maintainability, reusability, readability, and good software engineering practice.
Contribute to improvements in test processes, tooling, environments, test data management, and quality engineering practices.
Support non-functional testing activities, including performance, reliability, compatibility, and security testing where appropriate.
Communicate testing progress, risks, results, and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Essential Skills And Experience
Professional experience in software testing, test automation, quality engineering, software development, or a related role.
Strong programming experience in at least one language such as Java, C#, Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript, with the ability to write clean, maintainable, and reusable code.
Practical experience developing and maintaining automated tests for web applications, APIs, microservices, or other software systems.
Hands-on experience with test automation tools and frameworks such as Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, Appium, REST Assured, pytest, JUnit, NUnit, or equivalent.
Good understanding of software testing principles, including test design techniques, risk-based testing, regression testing, integration testing, and defect lifecycle management.
Experience working with version control systems, preferably Git, and contributing to collaborative development workflows such as pull requests and code reviews.
Experience integrating automated tests with CI/CD tools and pipelines, such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or equivalent.
Familiarity with API testing, HTTP, JSON, SQL, databases, and tools for inspecting and validating service responses.
Understanding of Agile software development methodologies, including Scrum or Kanban, and experience working within cross-functional delivery teams.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex failures and communicate technical findings clearly.
Good written and verbal communication skills, with a proactive, collaborative, and quality-focused approach to delivery.
Desirable Skills And Experience
Experience with advanced mobile automation capabilities, including Appium, device farms, parallel device execution, cross-device testing, or cloud-based mobile testing platforms.
Experience with AI-enabled testing capabilities such as self-healing automation, intelligent test generation, failure classification, or automated test maintenance
Experience using AI coding assistants or AI-enabled testing tools within a software development or test automation workflow.
Understanding of responsible AI usage, including validating generated code, protecting sensitive test data, and maintaining human oversight of automated testing decisions.
Experience with cloud platforms, containers, Docker, Kubernetes, or distributed systems.

About The Team
Read more about the research team's work here: https://decagon.ai/blog/introducing-decagon-labs
The Research team develops the model and decision-making stack that powers Decagon’s conversational agents for enterprise support. We research, adapt, and implement state-of-the-art techniques in model training, prompting, orchestration, and evaluation in order to make our agents more accurate, robust, and efficient in real-world deployments.
Our goal is to push the frontier of applied conversational AI: agents that reliably understand nuanced intent, track long context, and take the right actions under uncertainty. We measure success the way customers feel it: higher resolution rates, better user satisfaction, and consistent behavior at scale.
About The Role
As a Research Engineer focused on Safety, you’ll be responsible for making Decagon’s AI agents safe, reliable, and controllable, from evaluation through production. You’ll identify real-world failure modes and build the models, evaluations, and safeguards that prevent them.
We’re looking for strong engineers who want to advance applied AI safety in production. People here own their work end-to-end, ship real improvements, and are trusted to make high-impact technical decisions.
In this role, you will
Research and build safeguards against prompt injection, unsafe tool use, sensitive-data disclosure, policy violations, and hallucinated commitments
Build adversarial evaluations, simulations, red-team datasets, and regression suites informed by production failures
Develop and deploy classifiers, judges, reward signals, post-training methods, and runtime safeguards for safer agent behavior
Analyze production traces and incidents to identify root causes, test mitigations, and measure their impact
Partner with Security, Product, Infrastructure, Legal, and customer-facing teams to turn enterprise requirements into scalable safeguards and rollout practices
Your background looks something like this
2+ years of experience in AI/ML engineering, research, or AI safety
Hands-on experience evaluating, post-training, or deploying language models or agentic systems
Experience with modern post-training techniques, such as reinforcement learning, preference optimization, distillation, model routing, and synthetic-data generation
Experience with adversarial testing, model red teaming, prompt injection, policy enforcement, privacy, or safe tool use
Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling, with strong experimental judgment and the engineering depth to ship production systems
Comfort owning ambiguous, high-stakes technical problems and making clear risk and product tradeoffs
Even better if you have
Experience building safeguards for high-stakes or regulated enterprise workflows
Familiarity with human-in-the-loop review, incident response, or responsible rollout frameworks for ML systems
Compensation
$200K – $400K + Offers Equity
This range reflects the expected compensation for this role. Compensation within the range is determined based on experience, skills, and the scope of responsibilities, with flexibility for candidates who demonstrate exceptional impact.
In addition to base salary, we offer competitive equity. Final compensation may vary based on location within the United States.
Benefits

Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family
Life Insurance and Disability Benefits
Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K, pension)
Parental Leave
Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot
Monthly stipend to support your wellness, lifestyle, and work-life balance
Daily lunches and snacks in the office to keep you at your best
Take what you need vacation policy (subject to local requirements; UK employees receive 25 days of statutory leave)
These benefits are described in more detail in Decagon’s policies, may vary by location, and can change at any time according to applicable compensation and benefits plans.
Compensation Range: $200K - $400K

Define how AI agents operate in one of the world's largest advertising ecosystems — building agent orchestration, reinforcement learning from expert feedback, trust and permission systems, and scalable inference infrastructure that powers intelligent advertising decisions across Amazon Ads. This is a greenfield opportunity to give every advertiser, regardless of size or sophistication, access to the caliber of strategic campaign management previously available only through dedicated agencies.
Our team is developing an agent platform that coordinates multiple specialized AI sub-agents to execute complex, multi-step advertising workflows. You'll work with Applied Scientists on learning systems, partner with product teams on advertiser experience, and build the identity and authorization frameworks that keep it all secure. This is a small, high-ownership team where you'll ship fast, think in systems, and shape how AI transforms advertising from the ground floor.
Key job responsibilities
Develop orchestration systems that coordinate multiple specialized AI sub-agents to execute complex, multi-step advertising workflows
Build identity, authorization, and permission frameworks that enforce scoped access for diverse caller types
Implement feedback signal pipelines that capture expert judgment and route it into model improvement loops
Partner with Applied Scientists to integrate reinforcement learning from human expert feedback into production agent systems
Design and operate end-to-end evaluation systems that measure recommendation quality, detect regressions, and enforce quality gates
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (product, science, partner engineering) to define integration contracts and onboard new consumers to the platform
Own system reliability, observability, and performance for always-on agent infrastructure serving thousands of concurrent advertiser accounts
A day in the life
You might start the morning reviewing eval results from a newly onboarded agent skill, diagnosing why routing accuracy dropped 2%. By mid-morning, you're pairing with an Applied Scientist to tune the feedback pipeline that captures expert signals. After lunch, you're designing the permission model for a new integration. You end the day shipping an observability improvement that surfaces latency bottlenecks across the orchestration chain. We're a small, high-ownership team within Amazon Ads building the platform that makes AI agents accessible across the advertising ecosystem. 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Preferred Qualifications
3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Debug complex hardware/software issues, drive root cause analysis, and manage fixes through issue tracking systems (e.g., Jira).

Strong problem-solving, verbal, and written communication skills
Proficiency in Python and/or C

Git, GitHub, or Gerrit
Linux, Makefiles, GDB, IDEs, and bash scripting
ARM CPU, RISC-V, TrustZone, Caliptra, or Trusted Firmware

Job Title: Embedded Software Engineer
Job Description
This role focuses on developing embedded software for advanced radio systems used in edge communication products, enabling reliable military communications in signal-constrained environments. You will participate in the full software development lifecycle, work closely with hardware engineers, and contribute to secure, high-performance embedded solutions that operate in demanding real-time conditions.
Responsibilities
Participate in the full software development lifecycle, from concept and design through testing, integration, and deployment of embedded software for radio and edge communication systems.
Design, develop, and maintain embedded firmware using C and Python for microprocessor-based and microcontroller-based systems.
Write clean, well-structured, and well-documented embedded C code that adheres to industry best practices and coding standards.
Optimize firmware for memory utilization, power efficiency, and real-time performance to ensure reliable operation in constrained environments.
Leverage open-source technologies to support continuous integration, automation, and infrastructure management.
Build, maintain, and enhance CI/CD pipelines to streamline and automate software delivery and deployment.
Develop and maintain automated test frameworks to improve software quality and coverage.
Actively participate in code reviews, providing and receiving constructive feedback to maintain high engineering standards.
Troubleshoot and resolve issues related to interrupt handling, DMA operations, and peripheral interfaces such as SPI and I2C.
Interface directly with hardware peripherals and perform register-level communications and debugging.
Collaborate closely with hardware engineers to define interface requirements, integrate embedded software with hardware designs, and validate system functionality.
Use Texas Instruments development tools, including Code Composer Studio (CCS), or comparable environments to develop and debug embedded applications.
Utilize hardware debugging tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and JTAG debuggers to diagnose and resolve hardware–software integration issues.
Ensure embedded software solutions meet cybersecurity, security, and compliance requirements, aligning with DevSecOps principles where applicable.
Apply software architecture principles, including those used in microservices-based environments, to design robust and maintainable systems.
Use containerization technologies such as Docker to support development, testing, and deployment workflows.
Stay current with emerging technologies, software development methodologies, and industry best practices, and apply them to improve existing systems and processes.
Support programs related to defense or government applications, ensuring solutions meet mission-critical performance and reliability standards.
Essential Skills
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
3–5 years of professional experience developing embedded software in C for microprocessor-based systems.
Strong proficiency in Embedded C for firmware development on microcontrollers and microprocessors.
Hands-on experience with microcontrollers and bare-metal embedded development.
Experience working with SPI and I2C communication protocols and other peripheral interfaces such as UART.
Proficiency in Python for scripting and tooling related to embedded development.
Proficiency in Bash scripting for automation and development workflows.
Experience interfacing with hardware peripherals and performing communications at the register level.
Hands-on experience using Texas Instruments development tools, including Code Composer Studio (CCS), or similar embedded development environments.
Proficiency with hardware debugging tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and JTAG debuggers.
Experience developing and supporting CI/CD pipelines for embedded or software systems.
Familiarity with containerization technologies such as Docker.
Understanding of software architecture principles, including those applied in microservices-based environments.
Ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-documented embedded C code that follows established coding standards.
Active Secret Security Clearance.
Additional Skills & Qualifications
Experience developing software for real-time embedded systems, with a focus on performance and determinism.
Exposure to Linux-based embedded environments, including Embedded Linux and general Linux development.
Familiarity with automated testing frameworks for embedded or software systems.
Understanding of DevSecOps practices and their application to secure software development and deployment.
Experience supporting Department of Defense (DoD) or other government programs.
Knowledge of edge communication products and radio systems is beneficial.
Ability to stay up to date with emerging technologies and incorporate new methodologies and tools into existing workflows.
Work Environment
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement with an initial onsite focus to support effective onboarding and collaboration. The engineer will work onsite full-time during the first two months to become familiar with the hardware platforms, development tools, and team processes. After onboarding, the schedule transitions to approximately two days per week onsite, with the remaining time remote. The environment involves close collaboration with hardware and software engineers, regular use of embedded development environments, and hands-on work with lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and JTAG debuggers. The role supports mission-critical defense-related projects in a professional, engineering-focused setting that values security, quality, and continuous improvement.

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Warrent

Say hello to opportunities.
It’s not everyday that you consider starting a new career. We’re RingCentral, and we’re happy that someone as talented as you is considering this role. We invest more than $250 million annually to ensure our AI-enabled technology and platforms meet or exceed the needs of our customers.
RingSense AI is our proprietary AI solution. It’s designed to fit the business needs of our customers, orchestrated to be accurate and precise, and built on the same open platform principles we apply to our core software solutions.
Departmental Role & Strategic Impact
The Engineering department within RingCentral's Professional Services Delivery team is responsible for executing the technical implementation, configuration, and deep integration of RingCentral's solutions for customers across all segments.
This team acts as the technical engine of the delivery process. They bridge the gap between the initial sale and the final launch, turning high-level business requirements into fully functional, customized technical architectures — including AI-powered Unified Communications and Contact Center environments.
About The Role
The Professional Services Contact Center Engineer at RingCentral will drive the implementation of RingCX and RingCentral Contact Center (RCCC) functionality within new Contact Center designs, builds, and training. You will provide quality service to customers by ensuring the full benefits of the proposed solutions — including RingCentral's AI capabilities — are being delivered to them. This role is responsible for all technical aspects of project implementation and project management, executed to RingCentral standards and within agreed timelines.
Job Duties:
System Build & Implementation: Manage end-to-end technical implementation of RingCX and RingCentral Contact Center (RCCC) projects, including call flow configuration, IVR/ACD routing, dialer setup, and PBX/CTI integration.
Integrations & APIs: Connect RingCentral solutions to customers' existing systems using REST APIs and webhooks, syncing data with CRM and helpdesk platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, ServiceNow, and NetSuite.
AI-Enabled Solutions: Support the deployment of RingCentral's AI capabilities, such as AIRPro, within contact center implementations, helping customers realize the full value of AI-powered features.
Solution Design: Assess solution specifications against customer requirements and recommend designs or changes that optimize value for both the customer and RingCentral.
Project Delivery: Manage multiple concurrent implementations across customers, operating with minimal oversight, and keep timelines on track across requirements gathering, configuration, training, testing, and rollout.
Documentation: Complete customer-facing documentation throughout the implementation process, including meeting presentations, business requirements documents, and sign-off agreements.
Task Execution: Execute tasks and produce deliverables as outlined in the Project Plan and as directed by the Project Manager.
Status Reporting: Support the Project Manager with status reporting and escalation of issues.
Consultation: Provide technical consultation to customers, ensuring they realize the full benefits of their RingCentral solution.
Global Support: Support customers across multiple geographies, coordinating across time zones as needed.
Required Qualifications:
Education & Experience: BA/BS in a technical discipline or equivalent experience. Minimum of 2 years of experience in a Professional Services Implementation role; Contact Center industry experience is required.
Technical Expertise: Working knowledge of JavaScript, HTML,familiarity with logic based coding, networking; RESTful APIs; WFM; PBX; Dialer; ACD; CTI; VoIP; and IVR/VRU systems.
AI Familiarity: Basic familiarity with AI-enabled contact center capabilities (e.g., conversational IVR, AI-assisted QA, RingSense AI) and willingness to build AI fluency as RingCentral's AI feature set expands.
Problem-Solving Skills: Strong analytical skills, with the ability to identify, analyze, interpret, and resolve both practical and complex problems.

description_preview:
About Wonder
Everything’s on the menu at Wonder. Except compromise.
Wonder is the mealtime platform built to feed every craving in one order. With Wonder, you can mix and match hundreds of dishes from 20+ exclusive restaurants in a single order, so everyone gets exactly what they’re craving. Enjoy everything from tacos to Thai with $0 delivery fees, plus dine-in or pick up at a Wonder location near you. Each dish is made to order on-site by our culinary team and served hot.
Behind the scenes, Wonder owns and operates every step of the dining experience, from recipe development to the technology that powers our experience, allowing us to deliver quality, variety, and consistency at scale.
Join us as we work to make great food more accessible.
Within Wonder, the Robotics team is a core pillar of our innovation strategy. We build the automation solutions that help make Wonder’s 'no-compromise' promise possible at scale. Our mission is to use robotics to enable incredible variety and culinary authenticity. By reimagining the kitchen environment, we improve the daily experience of our team members and ensure every customer receives a perfect meal, every time.
The best in the business are coming to Wonder, working every day to make us the destination for every mealtime moment. Join a team of technology, culinary, and logistics pioneers, backed by top-tier venture capitalists, and help us make great food more accessible.
About The Opportunity
We are looking for a Robotics Software Engineer to bridge the gap between high-level orchestration and low-level machine control. In this role, you’ll develop robotics software to revolutionize the restaurant industry. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams. This includes software, hardware, and product development. You will design and build scalable software solutions. You should have experience working with software, electronics, and mechanical systems.
The ideal candidate will have experience working on real time software, share our passion for robotics reliability, and be excited to grow with us. If you love robotics and have a passion for food, we’d love to talk to you.
The Impact You Will Make
Pragmatic Problem Solving: Working with food can be a big challenge. The ideal candidate for this role will come at technical challenges with an open mind for creative solutions. You will utilize industry standards to implement new solutions within the robotics software suite.
High-Speed Feature Delivery: We move fast to launch new robotics products in a dynamic market. The ideal candidate will write clean, production-ready code quickly without sacrificing architecture or quality. You will balance rapid prototyping with scalable design to accelerate our development cycles.
Produce High Quality Software: We are proud of the phenomenal uptime we have on our existing robotics software infrastructure. The ideal candidate for this role will champion robotics software reliability. As part of this role, you will develop simulations and test suites that will ensure flawless delivery of software across hardware platforms.
Engineering at the intersection of Hardware and Software: As part of the robotics software team you will solve challenges that improve our restaurant technology. This includes development of new features within our Python Robotic control framework, adapting software to updated hardware designs, and improving machine reliability through robust machine error handling .
End-to-End Product Ownership: You will help build a brand-new robotics product from the ground up. This role offers the unique opportunity to leave your mark on a major new initiative. You will own core software components from initial concept to deployment to support, directly shaping the final product.
What You Bring To The Table
3+ years Python development experience in a workplace environment
2+ years experience in Robotics, Automation, Mechatronics or related field
Experience developing new software products, focusing on scalable and reliable system architecture
Experience programming scheduling/planning algorithms
Knowledge of networking principles
Experience applying Object Oriented design principles
Experience integrating software with new sensors/actuators
This role requires 4 days a week in the office. You're welcome—and encouraged—to be in the office up to 5 days a week if it works for you.
This role is based in our Boston office in Charlestown, MA
Massachusetts: $139,500 - $145,500 per year.
Wonder uses geographic-specific salary structures, which means the salary offered may vary depending on where the job is located. The final salary offer will take into account various factors, such as the candidate's skills, education, training, credentials, and experience.
Benefits

General Notes
The Center for Human and Robot Co-Adaptation (HRC) brings together six universities: The University of Texas at Austin, Indiana University Bloomington, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Tufts University, University of Utah, and Yale University. Together, we study how people and robots can, do, and might adapt to one another over months and years as needs, skills, expectations, and social contexts change. The Center unites researchers across robotics, AI, cognitive science, social science, data, and ethics to establish a new science of human-robot co-adaptation. This science will be developed, tested, and refined through the Human Environment with Robots (HERO) Facility Network: long-term deployments of assistive robots in real-world settings including student dorms, cafés, museums, homes, hospitals, and assisted-living facilities.
The Center is supported by a five-year, $30 million award from the National Science Foundation through its Science and Technology Centers (STC) program.
Purpose
The Center Robotics Software Engineer will develop, integrate, maintain, and deploy the common robotics software infrastructure that supports HERO deployments and foundational Center research. This position will create a standardized software stack that can support multiple robotic platforms and deployment sites, while providing researchers across the Center with reliable interfaces for developing, integrating, testing, and deploying new capabilities.
The successful candidate will be a strong software engineer with experience building and debugging complex robotic systems. They will work across research and engineering teams to translate rapidly evolving research software into robust deployable systems, while maintaining the testing, configuration, monitoring, and deployment infrastructure needed for long-running real-world robot operation. The engineer will be expected to take ownership of the Center's shared robotics software infrastructure, establish sound software engineering practices, and develop safeguards that allow new capabilities to be integrated without compromising the reliability of ongoing HERO deployments. The Robotics Software Engineer will work closely with the Robotics Hardware Engineer to coordinate platform integration, deployment readiness, troubleshooting, and upgrades across the Center’s robotic systems.
Responsibilities
Center Robotics Software Platform Ownership and Standardization
Own the architecture, integration, operational readiness, and maintenance of the Center's common robotics software stack.
Develop and maintain standardized software interfaces and configurations that support multiple robot platforms and can be replicated across HERO sites.
Establish common abstractions and interfaces for robot capabilities, sensing, communication, data collection, monitoring, and other shared functionality.
Evaluate new robotics software frameworks, libraries, models, and supporting technologies and recommend their adoption when appropriate.
Coordinate closely with Center researchers and the Center Robotics Hardware Engineer to ensure that the software infrastructure supports the scientific and operational goals of the Center.
Research Software Integration and Robotics Systems Engineering
Work with research teams across the Center to integrate new algorithms and capabilities into deployable robotic systems.
Develop and maintain ROS 2 packages, interfaces, launch systems, configuration infrastructure, and supporting software needed to connect research components into complete robotic applications.
Independently diagnose and resolve complex software failures spanning application code, middleware, operating systems, networking, drivers, dependencies, distributed computing, and hardware/software interfaces.
Design software architectures that allow experimental research components to evolve while maintaining stable interfaces and reliable operation of the overall system.
Support integration of computationally intensive capabilities, including perception, machine learning, foundation models, planning, and other AI systems running locally or on remote computing resources.
Reliability, Testing, and HERO Software Operations
Maintain the Center robotics software stack in a reliable and continuously deployable state.
Develop automated testing, continuous integration, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, monitoring, and validation systems to identify problems before deployment.
Establish staged deployment procedures, including simulation and digital-twin testing, local validation, canary deployments, and controlled rollout to HERO sites.
Develop logging, diagnostics, health monitoring, fault detection, and recovery mechanisms for long-running robot deployments.
Establish repeatable procedures for software installation, configuration, deployment, update, rollback, recovery, and validation.
Support diagnosis and resolution of software issues during HERO studies and deployments.
Multi-Site Software Deployment and Technical Coordination
Maintain common source repositories, software releases, configuration records, documentation, and deployment procedures for use across HERO sites.
Support replication and validation of the Center software stack across robot platforms and participating institutions.
Maintain configuration and version control across deployed systems while accommodating necessary site- and platform-specific differences.
Coordinate software releases and upgrades across sites to minimize fragmentation and maintain interoperability.
Work with researchers and local technical personnel to troubleshoot site-specific software, networking, computing, and deployment issues.

Edison Scientific builds and deploys AI scientist agents to accelerate science and the development of new medicines. We are an ambitious team run by scientists and engineers from leading institutions across biology, physics, chemistry, and AI.
The Role
As a Software Engineer on our Cloud team, you'll play a key role in building and scaling the technology powering our autonomous scientific discovery platform.
Our largest enterprise clients have compliance and security limitations which limit first-party data access to systems running within their own cloud infrastructure. These datasets are uniquely valuable assets; when combined with our scientific platform, Edison's enterprise partners are able to power novel drug or materials discovery campaigns at massive scale. The cloud team's mandate is to conquer the gnarly complexity that comes with these "bring your own cloud" engagements such that our platform is deployable within client cloud infrastructure.
Our mission is to build an AI scientist, and you'll be part of the team which enables Edison to scale to the largest research organizations in the world. You'll have significant ownership over the architecture and operations of our cloud deployment product, working alongside a small team of experienced engineers who care deeply about building world class software.
This role is on-site at our San Francisco office in the Dogpatch neighborhood. Our office is a converted warehouse with high ceilings, open space, and a team that genuinely believes in what they're building.
Responsibilities
Design, build, and operate the systems that make our platform deployable within client cloud infrastructure across AWS and GCP.
Develop operators, infrastructure tooling, and automation that streamline our bring your own cloud (BYOC) deployment process.
Support client deployments and onboarding hands-on, working directly with enterprise clients' engineering and security teams.
Partner with our forward deployed engineering team to scope requirements and deliver on inflight engagements.
Diagnose and solve bottlenecks in our BYOC process to streamline operations and expand our engagement capacity.

You will keep the robot systems, demos, teleop rigs, UMI data collection setups, cameras, grippers, and sensors running so the team can collect useful data and evaluate learned robot policies on real hardware.
This is not a pure lab manager role and not a pure technician role. You should be hands-on enough to wire, calibrate, fixture, debug, and operate robot cells, but technical enough to work closely with robot learning engineers, systems engineers, and controls engineers. Your job is to make sure experiments happen, demos stay ready, and the data that reaches the training pipeline is usable.
This is also not a pure ML job, but ML experience is required. You should be able to start training runs, run policy evaluations on the collected data and on the robot, and read the results well enough to tell the team whether the data or the policy is the problem.
You will be the on-site owner of the San Jose robot cells and will coordinate closely with the Trondheim lab so that both sites run the same collection protocols, calibration procedures, and data formats.
How You'll Move The Mission Forward
Own day-to-day readiness of robot learning lab systems: robot arms, grippers, cameras, trackers, force/torque sensors, safety equipment, and compute boxes.
Keep demos and data collection rigs operational, calibrated, documented, and ready for scheduled runs, including customer, investor, and partner demos at the San Jose office.
Run and support teleop data collection using VR headsets, trackers, robot controllers, and recording tools.
Support the UMI data collection by testing hardware, calibration, synchronization, ergonomics, and data quality in real collection sessions.
Collect high-quality robot demonstrations and autonomous execution logs across a broad and growing range of manipulation tasks, from machine-tending part handling to general pick, place, insertion, and reorientation.
Perform first-pass data QA: verify timestamps, camera views, robot state, action logs, task metadata, labels, and discard reasons before data enters the training dataset.
Work with the data platform team to make sure collected episodes upload correctly and carry the metadata needed for training, evaluation, and model lineage.
Work with robot learning engineers on what data is useful for VLA training, policy evaluation, recovery cases, and failure analysis.
Work with systems and controls engineers to debug policy execution, behavior tree integration, robot motion, safety stops, and runtime logging.
Design, fabricate, and maintain fixtures, mounts, adapters, test objects, and cell layouts for repeatable experiments.
Document setup procedures, calibration steps, collection protocols, failure modes, and lab operating practices, and keep them in sync with the Trondheim lab.
What You Need to Succeed
Hands-on experience building, operating, or maintaining robotic manipulation systems in a lab, company, or advanced academic setting.
Strong practical understanding of robot arms, grippers, cameras, sensors, calibration, and safety around physical robots.
Ability to debug real robot systems across hardware, software, networking, sensors, and operator workflow.
Programming ability in Python; enough C++ or ROS 2 familiarity to work effectively with robotics software engineers.
Comfort with data collection for robot learning: demonstrations, episodes, timestamps, camera streams, robot state, actions, labels, and quality checks.
Working ML experience: able to launch training runs from an existing pipeline, run evaluations, and interpret basic training and eval metrics.
Practical mechanical/electrical skills: wiring, mounting, 3D printing, fixture setup, connector troubleshooting, and basic CAD.
Clear documentation habits and the discipline to keep lab setups repeatable.
Business fluency in English.
Authorization to work in the United States.
What Will Differentiate You
Experience collecting data for imitation learning, diffusion policies, VLA policies, ACT, or similar robot learning methods.
Experience with teleop systems, VR controllers, motion trackers, UMI-style collection rigs, or learning-from-demonstration workflows.
Hands-on experience with industrial or collaborative robots such as Universal Robots, ABB, FANUC, KUKA, or similar.
Experience with camera calibration, multi-camera recording, depth cameras, wrist cameras, or vision-system debugging.
Familiarity with PyTorch, LeRobot-style datasets, RLDS, HDF5, Parquet, or other robot-learning data formats.
Experience deploying or evaluating learned policies on real manipulators.
Experience with industrial communication protocols such as Ethernet/IP, Modbus, OPC-UA, or vendor robot APIs.
Experience with CAD tools such as SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or Onshape, plus 3D printing or basic machining.
Experience working with a distributed team across time zones.
Why Join Us
You will own the lab systems that make robot learning real. When the team needs better data, a demo-ready cell, a calibrated teleop setup, or a policy tested on hardware, you are the person who makes it happen.
This role sits at the center of T-Labs' next six months: manipulation data collection, VLA model

Our advanced energy team is a dynamic division dedicated to powering the future through advanced electric vehicle (EV) battery systems and related electrified energy solutions. As we scale these advanced electrification initiatives, we are seeking technically strong engineers who can help establish the foundation for our product execution, safety strategy, and vehicle readiness.
In this position
The Battery Management Controls Software Engineer develops the application-layer control software that determines how a high-voltage battery system behaves: operating states, high-voltage sequencing, protection, limits, thermal control, diagnostics, and coordination across multiple strings.
Assignments may include supervisory system-level control software or string-level control software and may shift across the product architecture over the life of the program.
The ideal candidate has designed state machines, protection strategy, and diagnostic logic on a production program, works fluently in a model-based development environment with production code generation, and is comfortable debugging control behavior on real hardware.
What you'll do...
Develop and own operating state machines and mode management, including supervisory coordination across multiple controllers.
Implement high-voltage sequencing: precharge control and completion verification, contactor activation and deactivation, contactor diagnostics including welded and open contact detection, and interlock handling.
Implement protection strategy: cell and pack overvoltage and undervoltage, overcurrent, overtemperature and undertemperature, isolation loss, and thermal event detection and response.
Implement current and power limit calculation and arbitration, including derate strategy and coordination of limits across levels of the system.
Implement cell balancing demand logic and coordinate balancing behavior across modules and strings.
Implement thermal management control, including actuation, setpoint strategy, and thermal diagnostics.
Implement aggregation and consolidation of measured and estimated states for reporting at system level, and fault propagation and annunciation to external systems.
Own diagnostic strategy: fault detection, debounce, classification, storage, clearing, and reporting.
Integrate and calibrate estimation models delivered by algorithm engineering; own the calibration parameter set and its documentation.
Develop application software using model-based development with production code generation, plus hand-written C where appropriate.
Author software requirements and design documentation traceable to system requirements; support safety and security analyses.
Support validation debug, root cause analysis, and field issue resolution.
You'll have...
Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Computer, Mechatronics, Controls, or Mechanical Engineering.
5+ years developing embedded application or control software for electronic control units.
Model-based development proficiency with production code generation, plus working C ability.
Demonstrated state machine, sequencing, and diagnostic strategy design on a production program.
Requirements-driven software development with traceability, unit testing, and code review discipline.
Comfort working directly with hardware, benches, and instrumentation to debug control behavior.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability and willingness to travel occasionally.
Even better, you may have...
Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls, or a related technical field.
Battery management control software: contactor sequencing, protection strategy, limit calculation, and balancing.
High-voltage system experience and understanding of isolation, precharge, and interlock principles.
Software development under functional safety process requirements, including safety mechanism implementation.
Calibration methodology and parameter management for production programs.
Coordination or aggregation logic across distributed controllers.
Thermal management control strategy experience.

Model-based development and production code generation
Embedded C application software
State machine and mode management design
High-voltage sequencing and contactor control
Protection strategy and limit arbitration
Diagnostic strategy design
Thermal control strategy
Balancing demand logic
Calibration and parameter management
Requirements traceability and software documentation
Bench and hardware debug

title: Corporate AI Engineer
reason: Stack +19; Title fit +12; Poor fit -16; US +10; Overqualified -45; Senior salary -45
description_preview:
The Basics
The Corporate AI Engineer is a hands‑on technical role responsible for building, integrating, and operationalizing AI‑enabled solutions across the enterprise. This role focuses on delivery and execution, turning prioritized AI use cases into secure, scalable, production‑ready capabilities that drive measurable business value.
As a core AI-solution delivery member of Enterprise Architecture team, the Corporate AI Engineer partners closely with IT, Security, Data, and Business teams to move AI solutions from idea to pilot to measurable enterprise impact.
Join us if you are passionate about leveraging AI to drive meaningful outcomes and if you thrive in a growing, collaborative and innovative environment.
This position follows the Company’s hybrid schedule which currently requires employees to work in the office at one of the following locations a minimum of three days per week: Addison, TX; Bellevue, WA; Durham, NC; Emeryville, CA; or Reston, VA.
What You'll Do
Design, build, and deploy AI-enabled solutions aligned to prioritized use cases.
Implement AI workflows, integrations, and automations across enterprise platforms (e.g., Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow)using best-in-breed AI technology from Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.
Translate architectural designs and business requirements into working AI solutions, including prompt engineering, orchestration logic, retrieveal augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
Integrate AI solutions with enterprise data sources and systems of record, ensuring data quality, accuracy, and appropriate access
Own operational readiness of AI solutions, including monitoring, logging, performance tuning, and ongoing optimization.
Partner with Security, Privacy, and IT teams to ensure AI solutions comply with enterprise governance, risk, and compliance requirements.
Develop and maintain technical documentation, runbooks, and reusable implementation patterns.
We’re looking for someone with
4+ years of experience in software engineering, platform engineering, data engineering, application management, or a similar hands-on technical role.
Demonstrated experience building, integrating, or operating production systems in an enterprise environment.
Hands-on experience implementing AI-enabled solutions, including generative AI concepts such as prompt engineering, embeddings, or RAGwith best-in-class AI technologies from OpenAI, Anthropic, ServiceNow, Microsoft, etc
Experience working with APIs, integrations, MCPs, and enterprise SaaS platforms.
Working knowledge of AI-related risks, including data security, privacy, model limitations, and cost considerations.
About Tanium
Tanium is the Autonomous IT company. Driven by AI and real-time endpoint intelligence, Tanium Autonomous IT empowers IT and security teams to make their organizations unstoppable.
Many of the world’s leading organizations trust Tanium’s single, unified platform for endpoint management and security to innovate faster, stay resilient and move business forward with confidence, at scale. To learn how Tanium delivers Autonomous IT for unstoppable business – visit www.tanium.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
On a mission. Together.
At Tanium, we are stewards of a culture that emphasizes the importance of collaboration, respect, and diversity. In our pursuit of revolutionizing the way some of the largest enterprises and governments in the world solve their most difficult IT challenges, we are strengthened by our unique perspectives and by our collective actions.
As a global organization with stakeholders around the world, it’s imperative that the diversity of our customers and communities is reflected internally in our team members. We strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone feels they have opportunities to succeed and grow because we know that only together can we do great things.
Our commitment to excellence and innovation has earned us a place on the Forbes Cloud 100 list for ten consecutive years, and we continue to be recognized worldwide as a great place to work.
Each of our team members has 5 days set aside as volunteer time off (VTO) to contribute to the communities they live in and give back to the causes they care about most.
What You’ll Get
The annual base salary range for this full-time position is $154,000 to $200,000. This range is an estimate for what Tanium will pay a new hire. The actual annual base salary offered may be adjusted based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, location, education, skills, training, and experience.
In addition to an annual base salary, team members will receive equity awards and a generous benefits package consisting of medical, dental and vision plan, family planning benefits, health savings account, flexible spending account, transportation savings account, 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match, life, accident and disability coverage, business travel accident insurance, employee assistance programs, disability insurance, and other well-being benefits.
Tanium is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, protected Veteran status, or other legally protected categories. If you require a reasonable accommodation in searching for a job opening, completing an application, interviewing, or completing any pre-employment testing or requirements, please contact accommodations@tanium.com. For more information refer to the “Know Your Rights” poster which is available here - https://www.eeoc.gov/poster.
Please be aware of job offers coming from people claiming to be Tanium employees. Tanium employees will only use @tanium.com email addresses to communicate with you, will have video interviews with you, and will never ask you for money.

The Corporate AI Engineer is a hands‑on technical role responsible for building, integrating, and operationalizing AI‑enabled solutions across the enterprise. This role focuses on delivery and execution, turning prioritized AI use cases into secure, scalable, production‑ready capabilities that drive measurable business value.
As a core AI-solution delivery member of Enterprise Architecture team, the Corporate AI Engineer partners closely with IT, Security, Data, and Business teams to move AI solutions from idea to pilot to measurable enterprise impact.
Join us if you are passionate about leveraging AI to drive meaningful outcomes and if you thrive in a growing, collaborative and innovative environment.
This position follows the Company’s hybrid schedule which currently requires employees to work in the office at one of the following locations a minimum of three days per week: Addison, TX; Bellevue, WA; Durham, NC; Emeryville, CA; or Reston, VA.
What You'll Do
Design, build, and deploy AI-enabled solutions aligned to prioritized use cases.
Implement AI workflows, integrations, and automations across enterprise platforms (e.g., Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow)using best-in-breed AI technology from Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.
Translate architectural designs and business requirements into working AI solutions, including prompt engineering, orchestration logic, retrieveal augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
Integrate AI solutions with enterprise data sources and systems of record, ensuring data quality, accuracy, and appropriate access
Own operational readiness of AI solutions, including monitoring, logging, performance tuning, and ongoing optimization.
Partner with Security, Privacy, and IT teams to ensure AI solutions comply with enterprise governance, risk, and compliance requirements.
Develop and maintain technical documentation, runbooks, and reusable implementation patterns.
We’re looking for someone with
4+ years of experience in software engineering, platform engineering, data engineering, application management, or a similar hands-on technical role.
Demonstrated experience building, integrating, or operating production systems in an enterprise environment.
Hands-on experience implementing AI-enabled solutions, including generative AI concepts such as prompt engineering, embeddings, or RAGwith best-in-class AI technologies from OpenAI, Anthropic, ServiceNow, Microsoft, etc
Experience working with APIs, integrations, MCPs, and enterprise SaaS platforms.
Working knowledge of AI-related risks, including data security, privacy, model limitations, and cost considerations.
About Tanium
Tanium is the Autonomous IT company. Driven by AI and real-time endpoint intelligence, Tanium Autonomous IT empowers IT and security teams to make their organizations unstoppable.
Many of the world’s leading organizations trust Tanium’s single, unified platform for endpoint management and security to innovate faster, stay resilient and move business forward with confidence, at scale. To learn how Tanium delivers Autonomous IT for unstoppable business – visit www.tanium.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
On a mission. Together.
At Tanium, we are stewards of a culture that emphasizes the importance of collaboration, respect, and diversity. In our pursuit of revolutionizing the way some of the largest enterprises and governments in the world solve their most difficult IT challenges, we are strengthened by our unique perspectives and by our collective actions.
As a global organization with stakeholders around the world, it’s imperative that the diversity of our customers and communities is reflected internally in our team members. We strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone feels they have opportunities to succeed and grow because we know that only together can we do great things.
Our commitment to excellence and innovation has earned us a place on the Forbes Cloud 100 list for ten consecutive years, and we continue to be recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

General Notes
The Center for Human and Robot Co-Adaptation (HRC) brings together six universities: The University of Texas at Austin, Indiana University Bloomington, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Tufts University, University of Utah, and Yale University. Together, we study how people and robots can, do, and might adapt to one another over months and years as needs, skills, expectations, and social contexts change. The Center unites researchers across robotics, AI, cognitive science, social science, data, and ethics to establish a new science of human-robot co-adaptation. This science will be developed, tested, and refined through the Human Environment with Robots (HERO) Facility Network: long-term deployments of assistive robots in real-world settings including student dorms, cafés, museums, homes, hospitals, and assisted-living facilities.
The Center is supported by a five-year, $30 million award from the National Science Foundation through its Science and Technology Centers (STC) program.
Purpose
The Center Robotics Hardware Engineer will develop, integrate, maintain, and deploy the robots for HERO deployments and foundational research necessary to advance the strategic goals of the Center. This position will require integrating sensors, compute and additional components with off-the-shelf robotics systems to support deployments at multiple sites across the Center, and to develop a common set of integration and field operations procedures to ensure that the robots remain safe, reliable, maintainable, and continuously deployable for Center research.
A successful candidate will be a hands-on engineer with strong hardware and software expertise who can assemble systems based on desired functionality and operational constraints. They will have to independently assess the requirements, plan for integration of, and debug failures as necessary --- spanning mechanical, electrical, sensing, communications, driver, middleware, and application layers. The engineer will be expected to take ownership of the Center's robotic platforms, document their operation and maintenance, support their replication at Center sites, and develop safeguards that minimize the likelihood of failures. The Robotics Hardware Engineer will work closely with the Robotics Software Engineer to coordinate platform integration, deployment readiness, troubleshooting, and upgrades across the Center’s robotic systems.
Responsibilities
Center Robotic Platform Ownership and Standardization
Own the hardware and software integration, operational readiness, maintenance, and field deployment of mobile robotic platforms.
Develop and maintain standardized platform configurations that can be replicated across HERO sites.
Translate research and deployment needs into robot hardware, sensing, computing, communication, and integration requirements.
Evaluate new robot platforms, sensors, compute systems, and other technologies and recommend upgrades as Center needs and the state of the art evolve.
Coordinate with Center researchers and the Center Software Engineer to ensure platforms support the scientific goals of the Center.
Reliability, Deployment Readiness, and HERO Operations
Maintain Center robots in a safe, reliable, maintainable, and continuously deployable state.
Establish repeatable procedures for setup, calibration, configuration, inspection, transportation, deployment, recovery, maintenance, and repair.
Develop health checks, monitoring, startup validation, fault detection, and other safeguards to identify failures before deployment and prevent recurring problems.
Support and, when appropriate, lead technical field operations for HERO studies and demonstrations.
Diagnose deployment failures and coordinate recovery or repair with local site personnel.
Multi-Site Replication and Technical Coordination
Document reference platform configurations and support their replication and validation across HERO sites --- including integration diagrams, BOMs, installation guides and reference manuals.
Work with local facility personnel and researchers to troubleshoot site-specific hardware and deployment issues.
Maintain configuration control across platforms, including hardware revisions, firmware, software compatibility, calibration, and spare-part requirements.
Coordinate platform changes and upgrades across sites to minimize fragmentation and maintain interoperability.
Work closely with the Center Software Engineer and research teams on problems that cross hardware/software boundaries.

description_preview:
Job Title: Junior DSP Engineer
Job Description
The Junior DSP Engineer supports the development, testing, and analysis of advanced sensing and communications systems, working with real-world signals, laboratory equipment, data analysis, and algorithm development. This role is ideal for an early-career electrical or related engineer who wants hands-on experience with RF systems, digital signal processing, and laboratory and field-test activities. The position is based in Warrenton, VA and includes approximately 15% travel to customer sites, test events, and engineering demonstrations.
Responsibilities
Analyze and characterize complex waveforms collected from sensors, communications systems, and RF-based platforms.
Conduct laboratory testing, calibration, and validation of signal processing systems using oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and other RF test equipment.
Develop, model, and evaluate signal processing techniques using MATLAB, Python, or similar engineering tools.
Process and analyze large datasets to identify signal characteristics, system performance trends, and potential anomalies.
Support the development and refinement of filtering, detection, classification, tracking, and waveform analysis algorithms.
Collaborate with hardware, systems, and software engineers to troubleshoot signal integrity issues and validate overall system performance.
Participate in field testing activities and assist with data collection, system integration, and performance assessments.
Document test procedures, engineering analyses, and technical findings for internal teams and external stakeholders.
Support design reviews, technical briefings, and customer demonstrations by preparing technical content and participating in discussions.
Stay current with emerging technologies and industry trends related to digital signal processing, communications, sensing systems, and RF engineering.
Essential Skills
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.
0–5 years of experience in signal processing, communications systems, RF engineering, test engineering, or a closely related field.
Understanding of DSP fundamentals, including filtering, spectral analysis, sampling theory, FFTs, signal detection, and waveform characterization.
Experience using MATLAB, Python, or similar tools for data analysis, modeling, and visualization.
Familiarity with laboratory test equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, vector signal analyzers, network analyzers, and signal generators.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret real-world measurement data.
Ability to work effectively in both laboratory and field-test environments.
Willingness to travel approximately 15% for customer meetings, test events, and system demonstrations.
Active Secret Clearance or the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Clearance.
Hands-on experience or familiarity with RF concepts and RF test equipment such as signal analyzers.
Comfort working with Linux or embedded Linux environments in support of testing and signal processing tasks.
Additional Skills & Qualifications
Master's degree in a technical discipline with coursework focused on Digital Signal Processing, Communications, Radar, Electronic Warfare, or Applied Mathematics.
Experience analyzing RF, radar, communications, acoustic, sonar, or sensor-generated data.
Exposure to software-defined radio (SDR) platforms and associated signal analysis tools.
Familiarity with digital communications concepts such as modulation, demodulation, synchronization, and channel analysis.
Experience supporting laboratory experimentation, field testing, or prototype system development.
Knowledge of machine learning or advanced analytics applied to signal processing problems.
Experience with general RF laboratory tools and test setups.
Ability to collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary engineering teams and communicate technical concepts clearly in written reports and presentations.
Work Environment
This role is primarily based on site in Warrenton, VA, with an initial onboarding period during which the engineer works on site every day for the first two months to gain familiarity with systems, tools, and processes. After onboarding, the role transitions to a hybrid schedule with approximately two days per week on site. The work environment includes laboratory settings with RF test equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and other lab tools, as well as field-test environments for system integration and data collection. The position involves about 15% travel to customer locations, test events, and engineering demonstrations. Engineers collaborate closely with hardware, systems, and software teams, using technologies such as MATLAB, Python, Linux, and embedded Linux to support signal processing and testing activities.
Job Type & Location
This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Warrenton, VA.
Pay And Benefits
The pay range for this position is $50.00 - $70.00/hr.
Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.
Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific elections, plan, or program terms. If eligible, the benefits available for this temporary role may include the following:
Medical, dental & vision

Life Insurance (Voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents)

Systems Engineer (Command and Control / Maritime Systems)
Remote · Full-time
Pay: $94,717.13 - $140,067.94 per year
A blimp, a radar, and a camera are all watching the same stretch of water. Right now they each tell their own story. Your job is to make them tell one.
We are looking for a Systems Engineer to connect sensors like aerostats, radars, and cameras into the Navy's communications systems. All that information comes together in an operational picture, the single map that Navy watch teams use to see what is happening at sea. You help make that map complete and trustworthy.
Some travel comes with the job, including trips to partner countries to survey sites, test systems, and train the people who will use them.
Who you would help
You would support the office that builds and delivers these systems for allied partner countries. The goal is simple. Partner navies should be able to work side by side with US forces, and also handle things on their own. What you build gets used, not filed away.
What you would do
Systems engineering is a lot like solving a puzzle. You take pieces that were never made to fit together and you make them work as one.
Day to day, that looks like:
Connecting sensors, networks, and software so they talk to each other
Working across the whole build: planning it, designing it, coding it, testing it, and keeping it running
Turning what the customer needs into clear technical requirements
Visiting sites to see what is really there before you design around it
Running acceptance tests to prove the system works, then fixing what testing turns up
Training the partner teams who will operate and maintain what you install
Working with Navy staff, program leads, contractors, and other companies on the team
Good systems engineers keep one eye on the big picture and one on the details. You will think about cost and schedule too, not just the technology.
What we are looking for
At least 3 years of related systems engineering experience
A good grasp of systems engineering basics: figuring out requirements, designing the approach, putting the pieces together, and proving it works
Hands-on experience connecting different networks, software, and hardware
Comfortable working independently and traveling when the job calls for it
Bachelor's degree (required)
Active Secret clearance (required) that you can maintain. US citizenship is required.
Nice to have, but not required
Command and control systems, or other systems that build an operational picture
Work with radars, cameras, aerostats, or similar sensors
Network or RF design experience, including microwave and backhaul
Site surveys, installations, and system acceptance testing
Training end users, in a classroom or hands-on
NAVWAR, NIWC Pacific, or PEO C4I experience
Foreign Military Sales or work with partner countries
Writing government deliverables such as CDRLs
If you meet the main requirements and only some of these, apply anyway. The specific equipment is learnable. Knowing how to make systems fit together is the part that matters.
Why you might like it here
Your work shows up on a screen someone uses to make a real call. We are a small team, so you own your piece from start to finish instead of inheriting a slice of someone else's design. And you can do it from wherever you live.
